title: Is it okay to run shirtless in public?
description:
Do you run without a a shirt on ever? Lots of people have opinions on this topic and in some parts of the world it’s something you’re just not allowed to do.

We hear from runners around the world for their take on the decision to run without a shirt one - for both men and women.

And Yijin Shim from BBC Korean tells us about how in South Korea “no shirtless running” signs have been popping up after more runners have been going shirtless in a heatwave.

summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討民眾在公共場所赤裸上身或僅穿運動內衣跑步的爭議與各地規範。主持人 Hannah Gelbart 與來自英國、印度及美國的跑者交流，討論酷熱天氣下不穿上衣對散熱與防止磨擦的好處，同時剖析大眾對男女規範與體型觀感的雙重標準。節目亦提及義大利威尼斯與索倫托等城市禁止在非海灘區域裸露上身，違者最高可被處以 500 歐元罰款。此外， BBC 韓語服務記者 Yijin Shim 指出，南韓因酷暑使赤膊跑者增加，但部分民眾對此感到不適，首爾汝矣島漢江公園與南山公園等景點因而張貼宣導告示。節目最後提醒跑者在外地跑步前，應先了解當地的法律與文化規範。
summaryEn: In this episode of What in the World, host Hannah Gelbart explores the global debate surrounding running shirtless or in a sports bra in public places. Runners from the UK, the US, and India discuss how removing shirts during heatwaves helps with sweat evaporation and chafing while improving body confidence, though societal expectations and gender double standards persist. The podcast also examines local regulations, including fines of up to 500 euros for going shirtless away from beaches in Italian towns like Venice and Sorrento, as well as signs posted in South Korea's Yeouido Hangang River Park and Namsan Park requesting runners stay covered. Host Hannah Gelbart emphasizes the importance of checking local laws and social norms before running shirtless abroad.
